advances: For the genuine regular-simplex body, this performs an all-fiber canonical completion audit without replacing the canonical reservoir by the prescribed antipodal matching.  Every convexity-forced integer fiber enters through its actual volume in the parity totals and in the product weights.  The bad complete-\(h\)-uniform antipodal family has canonical reservoir share at most \(2/(3h^2)\), contributes at most \(1/4\) to target-zero congestion, and carries at most the same vanishing share of the actual load, positive-fresh charge, affine defect, or blocker packing.  If the canonical ledger is hard, more than \((99/100-2/(3h^2))Q\) of the load is forced onto the cross-pair/interior-fiber completion.  The proof also gives explicit lower bounds for each of the six hard-ledger capacities.  Thus the unbounded integrality gap of the selected antipodal blocker is not a canonical obstruction; any remaining obstruction must be proved on the completed edge system.
author: research-agent
proof:
The consecutive differences in the first half of the displayed base list are

\[
 p_{i+1}-p_i=2(1,i)
 \qquad(1\leq i\leq N-1),
\tag{35}
\]

and the missing closing step from \(p_N\) to \(-p_1\) is \(2(1,N)\).  The negatives supply the opposite directions in the same strict angular order.  Thus

\[
 p_1,\ldots,p_N,-p_1,\ldots,-p_N
\]

is the vertex list of a strictly convex polygon, so every displayed base point is exposed.  The fiber of a convex hull over an exposed base vertex uses only the corresponding displayed set.  This proves (15).  Also, for \(i<j\),

\[
 p_j-p_i
 =\bigl(2(j-i),(j-i)(i+j-1)\bigr).
\tag{36}
\]

The two factors in the second coordinate have opposite parity because their sum is \(2j-1\).  Hence both coordinates in (36) are even.  Moreover, \(-p_i\equiv p_i\pmod2\).  All displayed vertices therefore have one parity \(\zeta_*\).

Write

\[
 \widetilde C:=\operatorname{conv}
 \{(p_i,c_i^+),(-p_i,c_i^-):1\leq i\leq N\}.
\]

Equation (6) is exactly

\[
 C=\widetilde C+(\{0\}\times R_dB_d).
\tag{37}
\]

The base projection is \(P\).  If \(z\in P\), the fiber of \(\widetilde C\) over \(z\) is nonempty, and (37) shows that \(C_z\) contains a translate of \(R_dB_d\); it consequently has positive \(d\)-volume.  Outside \(P\) the fiber is empty.  Therefore \(Z=P\cap\mathbb Z^2\).  This proves assertion 1, including all interior and boundary lattice fibers forced by convexity.

If \(\zeta_*\) is bad, accepted fact `c81f02314cb34f8b` makes the canonical reservoir identically zero on that class.  Equations (11)--(13) and the edgewise bounds for the canonical optimizer and fresh charge then prove (16).

Suppose \(\zeta_*\) is good.  Equation (9), together with (15), gives the first equality in (17).  Since the all-fiber total satisfies \(A_{\zeta_*}\geq2Na\), summing over the \(N\) antipodal edges gives

\[
 q_{\mathrm{ant}}
 =\frac{Na^2}{4A_{\zeta_*}}
 \leq\frac a8.
\tag{38}
\]

The exact class contribution to the half-strength product reservoir is

\[
 Q_{\zeta_*}
 =\frac{A_{\zeta_*}^2-
 \sum_{z\equiv\zeta_*}a_z^2}
 {8A_{\zeta_*}}.
\tag{39}
\]

Goodness says \(\max_{z\equiv\zeta_*}a_z\leq A_{\zeta_*}/4\), so

\[
 \sum_{z\equiv\zeta_*}a_z^2
 \leq
 \left(\max_{z\equiv\zeta_*}a_z\right)A_{\zeta_*}
 \leq\frac{A_{\zeta_*}^2}{4}.
\tag{40}
\]

Equations (39)--(40), \(A_{\zeta_*}\geq2Na\), and \(Q\geq Q_{\zeta_*}\) prove (18).  Dividing (38) by (18) proves (19).  Notice that no interior fiber was discarded: its actual \(a_z\) occurs in both (39) and (40).

We next audit the six capacities.  Accepted fact `695b44a4f0fdcd3a`, applied to the actual full canonical reservoir and its load-minimal optimizer from accepted fact `6496cb3b0fd44f9d`, gives (20).  The branch assumption \(G<W/4<W/2\) allows the positive-fiber estimate of accepted fact `c81f02314cb34f8b`.  Applied to any displayed vertex fiber of mass \(a\), it gives \(a\leq G/4\), which is the first bound in (21).

For the selector bound, take the singleton base set \(E=\{p_1\}\), its fiber centroid \(c_1^+\), and weight \(\gamma_da\).  The centroid has absolute fiber depth at least \(\gamma_da\), as used in the centroid specialization of accepted fact `be359f8a6c628483`.  A singleton has base rank zero, and the affine map taking \(p_1\) to \(c_1^+\) gives residual rank zero.  The definition of \(R_{\mathrm{sel}}(C)\) in that accepted fact therefore gives

\[
 R_{\mathrm{sel}}(C)
 \geq2^2\gamma_da=4\gamma_da.
\tag{41}
\]

The same accepted fact gives \(D=2^2h_{\max}(C)\geq R_{\mathrm{sel}}(C)\).

Assume \(q_{\mathrm{ant}}>0\).  The centroid of the two endpoint fibers of \(e_i\) has base point zero and continuous point

\[
 \bar c_{e_i}:=\frac{c_i^++c_i^-}{2}=-\alpha u_i.
\tag{42}
\]

By part (a) of accepted fact `6b09aae189415c70`,

\[
 \sigma_{\mathrm{ant}}
 :=\sum_{i=1}^Nr_{e_i}\delta_{(0,-\alpha u_i)}
\tag{43}
\]

is a positive submeasure of an allowed exact minimum-unmatched centroid host.  Its base rank is zero.  The \(u_i\) are regular-simplex vertices with affine dimension \(N-1\), so its continuous residual rank is \(N-1\).  The accepted off-diagonal score is therefore

\[
 M_{\mathrm{off}}(C)
 \geq2^2\frac{|\sigma_{\mathrm{ant}}|}{N}
 =\frac{4q_{\mathrm{ant}}}{N}.
\tag{44}
\]

All edges in (10) are distinct reflected pairs about the integer fiber \(0\).  That fiber is positive because (37) puts \(-\alpha u_i+R_dB_d\) inside \(C_0\).  Part (b) of accepted fact `6b09aae189415c70`, again with affine centroid rank \(N-1\), gives

\[
 R_{\mathrm{cloud}}(C)
 \geq4\gamma_{2d}2^2
 \frac{q_{\mathrm{ant}}}{N}
 =\frac{16\gamma_{2d}q_{\mathrm{ant}}}{N}.
\tag{45}
\]

That accepted fact also gives \(D\geq M_{\mathrm{off}}(C)\) and \(D\geq R_{\mathrm{cloud}}(C)\).  Together with (41), this proves (22)--(23).  These are bounds, not claims that any lower bound is the exact value of its capacity.

By (15), the antipodal midpoint bodies are

\[
 L_{e_i}
 =\frac12(\mathcal K_{p_i}+\mathcal K_{-p_i})
 =-\alpha u_i+B_d.
\tag{46}
\]

The endpoint masses are both \(a\), so direct substitution in (12) gives \(\vartheta_{e_i}=a/2\).  Accepted fact `6496cb3b0fd44f9d` gives \(0\leq\omega_e\leq r_e\) for every edge.  Hence

\[
 \Omega_{\mathrm{ant}}
 \leq q_{\mathrm{ant}},
 \qquad
 \kappa_{\mathrm{ant}}
 =\frac{2\Omega_{\mathrm{ant}}}{a}
 \leq\frac{2q_{\mathrm{ant}}}{a}
 \leq\frac14.
\tag{47}
\]

Equations (19) and (47) prove (25).  Since \(0<\chi_0\leq1\), equation (13) proves (26).  If \(\chi_0<1\), then the definition in (12) forces \(\kappa_0>1\), and therefore

\[
 \kappa_{\mathrm{comp},0}
 =\kappa_0-\kappa_{\mathrm{ant}}
 >1-\frac14=\frac34.
\tag{48}
\]

If \(\chi_0=1\), (13) gives \(B_{\mathrm{ant}}=0\).  This proves assertion 4 using the actual full target multiplier, whose completed contribution is retained in \(\kappa_{\mathrm{comp},0}\).

It remains to verify the blocker claim.  The regular-simplex identities are

\[
 \lVert u_i\rVert_2=1,
 \qquad
 \langle u_i,u_j\rangle=-\frac1{N-1}\quad(i\ne j),
 \qquad
 \sum_i u_i=0.
\tag{49}
\]

For a subset \(J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}\) of size \(s\), write \(\bar u_J=s^{-1}\sum_{i\in J}u_i\).  Expanding (49) gives

\[
 \lVert u_i-\bar u_J\rVert_2=f_s
 \qquad(i\in J),
\tag{50}
\]

and, for every \(x\in H_1\),

\[
 \frac1s\sum_{i\in J}
 \lVert x+\alpha u_i\rVert_2^2
 =\lVert x+\alpha\bar u_J\rVert_2^2
 +\alpha^2f_s^2.
\tag{51}
\]

The minimum possible value of \(\max_{i\in J}\lVert x+\alpha u_i\rVert_2\) is therefore \(\alpha f_s\), attained at \(x=-\alpha\bar u_J\).  Since \(f_s\) is increasing in \(s\), (2) and (46) show

\[
 \bigcap_{i\in J}L_{e_i}\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 |J|\leq h-1.
\tag{52}
\]

Every edge in (10) has the same base target zero, so an affine map hits a chosen subfamily exactly when its value at zero belongs to the corresponding intersection in (52).  The inclusion-minimal non-hit families are consequently the \(h\)-subsets.

By (28), the total positive-fresh capacity on the antipodal family is exactly \(B_{\mathrm{ant}}\).  Nonnegativity gives (30).  If \((\zeta_I)_{|I|=h}\) is any feasible fractional packing of the complete \(h\)-uniform blocker family, summing its edge-capacity constraints yields

\[
 h\sum_{|I|=h}\zeta_I
 \leq\sum_{e\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{ant}}}\beta_e
 =B_{\mathrm{ant}}.
\tag{53}
\]

Taking the supremum proves (31).  The edgewise no-reuse convention is the one formalized in accepted fact `fd621e3189426c0d`; any nonnegative antipodal subcharge dominated by \(\beta\) has total at most the right side of (53).  Equations (26), (30), and (31) prove assertion 5.

Finally assume (32).  It implies separately \(R<Q/100\) and \(G<Q/100\).  Equations (20) and \(R<Q/100\) give

\[
 \Omega>\frac{99Q}{100}.
\tag{54}
\]

Equations (21), \(G<Q/100\), and the two cases (16)--(17) give

\[
 4a\leq G<\frac Q{100},
 \qquad
 q_{\mathrm{ant}}\leq\frac a8<\frac Q{3200}.
\tag{55}
\]

Combining (19) and (55) proves (33).  Since \(\Omega_{\mathrm{ant}}\leq q_{\mathrm{ant}}\), subtracting (33) from (54) proves (34).  This completes the all-fiber canonical completion audit and the proof.
